title: Evaluating LLM Uncertainty in Long-Form Generation Using Deterministic Ground Truth
research_question: How can uncertainty in long-form LLM generation be evaluated at fine-grained resolution without noisy external judges, and what does such evaluation reveal about correctness propagation, calibration, confidence ranking, and reasoning?
methodology: The paper introduces SALT, a procedurally generated benchmark in which long outputs have deterministic reference answers that can be decomposed into task-aligned atomic and line units. Six tasks with complete model coverage provide 54,797 evaluated atoms across mathematics, logic, code, DNA translation, and multi-needle retrieval, with additional ARC-AGI and maze experiments reported separately; more than 50 LLMs are evaluated. Unit correctness is determined against deterministic ground truth, while uncertainty is measured using precision, expected calibration error, Macro- and Micro-AUROC, PRR, multiple logit- and verbalization-based confidence functions, post-hoc calibration schemes, paired statistical tests, and controlled prefix interventions.

key_findings.finding: Fine-grained confidence ranking deteriorates sharply at atomic resolution: many models' atomic Micro-AUROC values lie only modestly above chance, while line-level units exhibit substantially clearer ranking signal.

Long-form correctness is path-dependent: errors in the generated prefix strongly reduce future correctness, while answer-context length contributes a separate but bounded degradation that saturates relatively early.

Reasoning interventions improved answer precision but reduced the model's ability to rank its own correct and incorrect units by confidence; the reported paired analysis found a 23.3 percent relative AUROC degradation alongside accuracy gains.

Logit-derived confidence functions significantly outperformed verbalized confidence across both calibration and ranking comparisons, but the best confidence function depended on which uncertainty property was being measured.
Post-hoc binned calibration minimized ECE but harmed ranking, demonstrating that calibration quality and error-ranking quality can move in opposite directions.

Uncertainty-estimation rankings transferred only conditionally to conventional benchmarks: line-level agreement was stronger for AIME, while agreement with MMLU-Pro was weak and depended on the calibration regime.

limitations: SALT's deterministic tasks are deliberately structured and synthetic, so they do not reproduce the ambiguity, conflicting evidence, source attribution, and open-ended semantics of real-world free-form reports.
Strict deterministic unit matching is much easier to define than factual correctness for naturally written multi-source claims.
The benchmark studies uncertainty on generated answer units but does not directly evaluate evidence completeness or whether decision-relevant source facts were omitted.
It does not directly model temporal evidence evolution, version supersession, or non-stationary source distributions.
ARC-AGI and Maze had incomplete model coverage because of compute constraints and were excluded from aggregate main-body results.
Transfer to external benchmarks was conditional, with weak agreement in some benchmark and granularity combinations.
The work evaluates uncertainty metrics rather than providing formal selective-prediction or risk-control guarantees under distribution shift.
raw_claims: SALT uses deterministic long-form targets so correctness labels do not depend on human or LLM judges.
The six tasks used for the aggregate evaluation contain 54,797 atomic units.
The study evaluates more than 50 language models.
Correctness tends to decrease as a generated response progresses.
The correctness of earlier generated units is strongly associated with the correctness of later units.
Controlled interventions separate error propagation from the effect of answer-context length.
Atomic-level confidence ranking is substantially weaker than line-level ranking.
Reasoning improves answer accuracy while degrading confidence-based discrimination between correct and incorrect units.
Logit-based uncertainty signals outperform verbalized confidence signals in the reported comparisons.
Optimizing post-hoc calibration for low ECE can reduce AUROC ranking quality.
The released repository includes reproduction datasets and procedural dataset generators.
